title: The chosen open-extension adjunction unit is invertible
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], and let $W\subset X$ be open. Let $L$ be the extension-by-zero presheaf functor [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] followed by module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and let $R$ be restriction to the slice site over $W$. For every sheaf $G$ of modules on that site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the component $G\longrightarrow R(LG)$ of the unit of the adjunction $L\dashv R$ chosen by [lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact] is an isomorphism of module sheaves.

source.place: Sheaves Tag 00A7 (lemma-j-shriek-modules), (4); Modules on Sites Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero)

proof.text: Use the canonical extension/restriction adjunction given by the direct-sum injections and module sheafification. For each open V contained in W the set of inclusions V into W is a singleton; hence the corresponding section module of the extension presheaf is canonically G(V), and its restriction maps agree with those of G.

Restriction of sheafification to W is sheafification of the restriction. The restricted presheaf just identified with G is already a sheaf, so the canonical unit is an isomorphism. This also covers the empty open and the total open.

Compare the canonical adjunction with the chosen adjunction by uniqueness of left adjoints. Their common left adjoint has a natural automorphism intertwining the units. Restriction preserves that automorphism, so the chosen unit component is also invertible.

proof_origin.place: Sheaves Tag 00A7 (lemma-j-shriek-modules), (4); Modules on Sites Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero)
